price_identity.why: the series is a BACK-ADJUSTED continuous contract: every roll subtracts a gap from all prior history, so the further back a row is the larger the accumulated adjustment. Confirmed three ways: the offsets are monotone in age with ~50 distinct levels; 395 of 416 rows have an IDENTICAL exit-minus-entry difference (an additive offset cancels in a difference); and prev_close_loc, which is offset-INVARIANT, agrees far more often than the ratio features that are not.
price_identity.so: the contract is confirmed. The absolute price level of older rows is not reproducible from today's parquet BY DESIGN, and the existing reproduction test still passes because it checks the current window.

a_measurement_error_of_mine_and_how_it_w.what: the first run used `_naive(df.index)`, which STRIPS the zone without converting
a_measurement_error_of_mine_and_how_it_w.but: the parquet index is UTC — `track1_live_source.frozen_frame` says so in a comment written after an earlier incident
a_measurement_error_of_mine_and_how_it_w.effect: every bar read four or five hours off; 420 of 421 entries mismatched
a_measurement_error_of_mine_and_how_it_w.the_tell: the parquet values carried a long decimal tail (9184.872880047082) where the artifact was round (8753). A price that cannot be a tick is a measurement fault, not a data fault.
a_measurement_error_of_mine_and_how_it_w.lesson: it is the exact mistake my own note warns about — measure in the frame the system uses, through the loader the system uses

grace.why: an OBSERVATION change, not a strategy one. A one-minute bar stamped 10:00 closes at 10:01:00, so 60s put the deadline exactly on the closing instant. Three minutes let a slot observe a CLOSED bar and still refuse anything past 10:03.
grace.entry_price: unchanged — still the OPEN at 10:00, asserted against CalmAParams.entry_time

part_C_fix.the_caller_was_wired_too: the gate change alone did nothing: the slot passed only the resampled 5-minute frame, so every Calm slot would have refused `entry_quote_unverified` instead of `decision_bar_absent` — a different refusal, not a fix. The joined 1-minute frame was already in scope at the call site and is now passed as the quote index.
part_C_fix.no_late_entry: too_late still refuses past the grace, and a refused slot is SLOT_REFUSED, never NO_SIGNAL — pinned
part_C_fix.partial_bar_constraint: held BY CONSTRUCTION: the context span stops at 09:55, so a 10:00 bar in the frame is outside everything the decision reads. Proved by verdict equality — adding a partial 10:00 bar with absurd high/low/close changes neither the verdict nor the span detail.

can_PAPER_SHADOW_EVIDENCE_count_calm.in_the_schedule: NOT YET, and this is the honest part. The slot is dispatched at 10:00:00 and the quote it needs closes at 10:01:00. Measured today at 10:00:19: MES's joined frame ended 09:59 while MNQ's already carried a 19-second-old 10:00 bar. The sleeve takes the first instrument's index, so it would still refuse.
can_PAPER_SHADOW_EVIDENCE_count_calm.what_would_fix_it: dispatch the Calm slot at 10:01 or 10:02 instead of 10:00. The entry price is unchanged, so this is an observation-time change, not a strategy change. It is a scheduler cron edit and needs a restart, so it is RECOMMENDED here and NOT applied.
